title: PagerDuty suppression window with correlated trace snippets and automated handoff summaries
creator: Avery Kumar
description:
Problem: During high-throughput incidents we see PD alert storms for the same underlying root cause (e.g. kernel OOM, KV cache pressure) resulting in alert fatigue and expensive oncall churn. Current PD alerts create separate incidents even when traces and metric patterns are correlated; oncall handoffs lack concise context (top traces, correlated errors, recent deploys) so follow-ups are slow.

Proposal: Implement a Pd-suppression-and-handoff service that:
- opens a short suppression window (configurable by rule) when we detect a burst of related alerts from the same logical service/component, so we avoid duplicate PD escalations for the same root cause while still creating a single canonical incident.
- runs a correlation pass that groups alerts by fingerprint (service, route, error class, metric signature) and attaches compressed trace snapshots (top spans, KV cache hit/miss indicators) to the canonical incident.
- auto-generates a Slack-thread handoff summary message with key traces, ingestion-safe excerpts (PII redacted), recent deploy hash, and recommended runbook steps. The Slack message includes buttons: Add runbook excerpt, Mark investigated, Create follow-up ticket.
- emits a compact postmortem skeleton to speed post-incident docs: initial timeline, top traces, affected endpoints and estimated error volume.

Design notes and constraints:
- Correlation engine will reuse the existing trace-hash algorithm from tracing-hooks service but include a fingerprint layer that normalizes request path parameters and maps error taxonomy to standardized codes.
- Trace snapshot must be limited to 3 spans max + a 4-line summary; any stderr/log excerpt included must be sanitized via existing log-redaction pipeline.
- Suppression windows are per-customer-tier and per-service; default 2 minutes for P0 bursts, 30s for P1, configurable in console.
- PD incident lifecycle: canonical incident opened immediately for the first alert that meets criteria; subsequent alerts are attached (not new incidents) unless a cooldown expires. We will follow PD best practices for incident urgency and responder escalation.

Success criteria / metrics:
- Reduce duplicated PD incidents by >=40% for correlated burst classes within 3 months of rollout.
- Mean time to first actionable context (time between PD page and Slack handoff summary) < 90 seconds.
- Oncall satisfaction survey improvement in the two teams piloting the feature.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement correlation + suppression in staging. 2) Pilot with infra-sre and runtime-serving teams for low-volume service groups for 2 weeks. 3) Expand to all runtime services with opt-out per-service toggle in Console. 4) GA and include in runbook library.

Backward compatibility & safety:
- Default behavior is off for all services; feature flag gate in Console and ff-rollout via config.
- If correlation service fails, system falls back to current PD behavior (no suppression). Fail-open semantics ensure alerts are not lost.

Open questions:
- Exact fingerprint hashing tolerances (how much path normalization) — need input from product on user-visible trace context.
- UI controls in Console for configuring suppression windows and per-service policies.

Expected deliverables:
- Pd-suppression-and-handoff microservice (k8s service), correlation ruleset, trace snapshot exporter, Slack message templates, Console toggles, unit & e2e tests, runbook templates, documentation and postmortem skeleton generator.
